 First Alert Weather Day: Flash flood warning canceled for East Maui, Hawaii Island 
 Conditions are expected to improve Thursday or Friday, with trade winds returning this weekend. By Ben Gutierrez , Jennifer Robbins , Guy Hagi , Dan Cooke and Billy V Published : Oct. 25, 2026 at 2:44 PM HST | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - A Flash Flood Warning was allowed to expire for Maui and Hawaii Island Thursday.
 As of 7:18 p.m., the National Weather Service said there are no watches, warnings or advisories.
 The warning was previously posted for windward portions of Hawaii Island as an area of moisture lingered over the eastern part of the state.
 Meanwhile, a flash flood warning was canceled for East Maui as heavy rainfall has diminished in that area.
 Your HNN First Alert Weather Team has declared Thursday a First Alert Weather Day for the islands of Maui County and Hawaii. 
 Hana High and Elementary School in East Maui were closed Thursday due to heavy rain and road closures. 
 Hawaii has seen beneficial rain overall with some heavy pockets that creating minor flooding but nothing major (hnn) Hawaii has seen beneficial rain overall with some heavy pockets that creating minor flooding but nothing major (hnn) Improvement expected Friday
 Improving conditions and drier air have already moved in over the islands of Kauai and Oahu. Some improvement is also anticipated for Maui County and Hawaii Island into the night, but some localized heavy rain will still be possible into Friday for areas of windward East Maui and windward Hawaii Island. More stable conditions should prevail by Friday afternoon statewide.
 Weather for Halloween trick-or-treating could still be wet, with scattered showers mainly for windward and mauka areas for the eastern end of the state.
 More typical trade winds briefly return but at times wet trades passing over the state (hnn) Your First Alert Weather Team will closely monitor conditions and First Alert you to any changes.
